findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 48 mm is observed in the tail of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. No other local invasion factors are identified. No lymph node metastases are present. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the image findings, the local invasion factors are:

CH0, DU0, S1, RP1, PV0, A0, PL0, OO0

Explanation:
- CH: No involvement of the common hepatic artery (CH0)
- DU: No involvement of the duodenum (DU0)
- S: Serosal invasion (S1)
- RP: Retropancreatic tissue invasion (RP1)
- PV: No involvement of the portal vein (PV0)
- A: No involvement of the abdominal aorta (A0)
- PL: No involvement of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels (PL0)
- OO: No involvement of the omentum (OO0)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the local invasion factors, the T classification is T3.

Explanation:
- T3: Tumor extends beyond the pancreas, but without involvement of major vessels (serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion meet this criterion).

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer are:
- Head: Stations 12a, 12b, 12c, 12d
- Body and tail: Stations 13, 14, 15, 16, 17

No lymph node metastases are present, so N classification is N0.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

No distant metastases are observed, so M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the T classification (T3) and M classification (M0), the tumor is not unresectable due to distant metastasis. However, the presence of serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion may make the tumor borderline resectable. Therefore, the resectability classification is Borderline Resectable (BR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T3), N classification (N0), and M classification (M0), the overall stage is Stage IIA.
